  "text": "The letters were warm. Ada closed her fingers around them before Elias could see, but something moved beneath her skin, arranging itself against her palm.

“Don’t read it,” Venn said.

“I haven’t.”

The brass plate shuddered. From the stairwell came the soft scrape of a shoe on the next step. The constable raised his lantern, illuminating nothing but peeling wallpaper.

Ada opened her hand. Six letters lay there, bright as coins. She knew the word they made. It had been spoken at Mara’s funeral, though no one had understood why Mara had asked for it to be carved beneath her own name.

Behind the door, the voice sighed. “She remembered.”

Ada looked at the warning on the yellow paper. Don’t answer until it asks to leave. Mara had left instructions, not a promise that they would be safe.

She set the letters on the floor, one at a time, spelling the name aloud. With each syllable, a scratch vanished from the door. On the final one, the stairwell gave a long, hollow creak.

The little gate in the plate swung wide. Through it Ada saw rain falling across an empty street.

“Is it gone?” the constable whispered.

Venn leaned toward the opening. Ada caught his sleeve before he could touch it.

At the bottom of the stairs, someone knocked on the front door: six patient blows.

Then Mara’s voice called up to them, no longer pleading. “Ada? I think you’ve let me out.”"
